\begin{restated}{Proposition}{prop:B3-lower}{B3}{1}{lower bound for SAGA with any constant step}
Let $n\ge1$, $0<\mu<R^2$, $d=2$, and $f_i(\theta)=\frac12(\mu\theta_1^2+R^2\theta_2^2)$ for all $i\le n$. Assumption~\ref{ass:B3-setting} holds with these constants, $F=f_1$, $\Fp(\theta)=Q\theta$ with $Q=\diag(\mu,R^2)$, and $\etastar=0$. Run SAGA~\eqref{eq:B3-saga} with any constant step $\gamma>0$ (which may depend on $\mu$) and any deterministic initial memory $z^{(0)}$. Then for all $t\ge0$,
\begin{equation*}\tag{\ref*{eq:B3-lower}}
\E[\theta_t]=(I-\gamma Q)^t\theta_0\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\E\norm{\theta_t-\etastar}^2\ \ge\ \norm{\E[\theta_t]-\etastar}^2\ \ge\ \Big(\frac{\kappa-1}{\kappa+1}\Big)^{2t}\min\{\theta_{0,1}^2,\theta_{0,2}^2\}.
\end{equation*}
In particular, for $\theta_0=(r,r)$ with $r\ne0$ and $\varepsilon<\frac12$, reaching $\E\norm{\theta_t-\etastar}^2\le\varepsilon\norm{\theta_0-\etastar}^2$ requires $t\ge\frac{\kappa-1}{4}\log\frac1{2\varepsilon}$, whatever the step.
\end{restated}
